Precise faults stop at the exact faulting instruction with the registers committed, at roughly 2x the cost on 32-bit code. Fast mode reports the end of the translated block instead and runs quicker - most apps do not notice, but a few report a crash at the wrong place.

The app is designed in Material 3, with one fixed palette - Google\'s own - so it looks the same on every phone. Pick the scheme you want to read it in; the icons, rows and switches are identical either way.
How a translated (32-bit) app is run. These are the defaults a new import starts with; any app can be changed afterwards by long-pressing it in the library.

On: a memory fault stops at the exact instruction with the guest registers committed, and the crash report says where it really happened. It costs roughly 2x on 32-bit code. Turn it off to make translated apps faster - the fault is then reported at the end of the translated block.
Whole-framebuffer readbacks, per-draw pixel diffs and ASCII frame maps in the run report. Debugging only, and very slow. Leave it off unless a window is black and you need to know why.
Hide ads in newly imported apps
Ad SDK views cannot work for a translated app and only leave empty banners. This hides them as soon as the app is imported; it never removes an ad from anything else.

Every window event, the runtime\'s own report as it changes, and the reason each process died, written to files/zb-app-log.txt and logcat. On by default; turning it off makes a session lighter (the report is not read every few seconds) and leaves only errors on logcat.
This APK is the release build, which compiles the detailed log out entirely - it is the debuggable build that writes one. See README-DEBUG-BUILD.md.

The :guest process rewrites files/zb-runtime-report.txt whenever the report changes, so a guest that dies silently still leaves its own account behind. Off means less I/O in a session and nothing to read after a crash.
Reopen the app when the guest process stops unexpectedly
A watched :guest process that dies with a window on screen is reopened by the launcher, at most three times in ten minutes. Off means a crash leaves the game closed.
A launch that fails while the app is installed is retried once in a fresh :guest process, which is what fixes the intermittent failures. Off means the reason is shown immediately.
Copy the reason to the clipboard when a launch fails
Makes the failure report pasteable on a phone with no file manager and a ROM with no usable logcat.
Every report here is also copied to the clipboard, so it can be pasted into a message without a file manager.
